LMP3.title: Norma M30 wins first race as YMR takes LMP3 1-2
LMP3.dek: Capo and Creed's M.Racing - YMR Norma M30 won by a lap from the team's Ligier, Ultimate third, while United's Ligiers lost out to contact and a gearbox problem.

chapters.title: A big class with two Normas
text: LMP3 reached Monza as the largest class on the grid, seventeen cars strong and all Ligier JS P3s apart from the Normas of M.Racing - YMR and Oregon Team. Silverstone had belonged to United Autosports: Falb and Rayhall's #2 won by a lap, Ultimate's #17 was second and the #3 of Patterson, Boyd and England third. YMR ran its #19 Norma with only Capo and Creed this time, Ehrlacher being away on WTCC duty, while Oregon, the one Italian team in the class, came to its home round after a heavy crash at Ascari during the Prologue.

The line-ups shifted elsewhere. Coigny returned to Cool Racing's #4 to make a trio with Alexander and Forgione, Duqueine added Légeret to the #8, and Mediani took Jensen's seat in AT Racing's #9 because Jensen was racing at Silverstone. Practice was tight. Eurointernational's Mondini led Friday's first session on 1:46.606, with Boyd's #3 and Rayhall's #2 separated by five thousandths in second and third. On Saturday morning YMR's Ligier #18 went quickest on 1:46.527, Mondini was second and Oregon's Norma third, with eight cars inside a second.

chapters.title: Boyd takes pole by 0.048s
text: The ten-minute session was settled in its closing minutes. Boyd put the United #3 on pole with a 1:45.725, only 0.048 clear of Capo's Norma #19, so the new chassis shared the front row. Lahaye's Ultimate #17 was third on 1:46.022, followed by Rayhall's #2, Cougnaud's #18 and Droux's Duqueine #7, which made the top six separate by less than half a second.

Mondini's #11 was seventh and Capitanio put the second Norma, the Oregon #10, eighth in class. At the other end, Pialat's Eurointernational #12 was the slowest of the 17, 2.380 seconds off pole on 1:48.105, and was gridded 30th overall among the GTE cars.

chapters.title: Contact shapes the early race
text: Incidents, not pace, decided the first half of the class race. Panis Barthez's #16 over-reached on AT Racing's #9 and the contact brought out the first of three Full Course Yellows; all three, including the second during Hour 2, were caused by LMP3 incidents.

The #9 was hit again by United's #2 when Rayhall misjudged a pass, and both cars ran through the gravel. Rayhall rejoined, but the Silverstone winners then had a gearbox problem, and the #9 ended the day with just 17 laps. Oregon's Norma #10 lost its front end by braking too late at the first chicane and was caught up in more incidents once repaired, and Cool Racing's #4, By Speed Factory's #5, Duqueine's #8 and Eurointernational's #12 also had their moments.

chapters.title: Boyd mounts a fightback
text: United's #3 slipped back in the middle of the race while Patterson raced the other teams' professionals, but Boyd then came through the field in a hard run towards the podium. RLR's Farano spun while reacting to the Oregon Norma ahead of him, which cost the #15 time, and Mondini's iron-man stint in Eurointernational's #11 ended with cramp, leaving fifth as the best the car could save. Inter Europol's #13 fell behind Boyd's charge but held sixth, a good return for a hard afternoon.

chapters.title: YMR 1-2, Ultimate third
text: Creed took the chequered flag in the #19 Norma one lap clear of the team's Ligier #18, which had made a late charge in Cougnaud's hands. Ultimate's #17 completed the podium about half a minute behind the Ligier on the same lap, Jean-Baptiste Lahaye, Matthieu Lahaye and Heriau sharing the car. Boyd's rally ran out just short of the rostrum in fourth, ahead of the Eurointernational #11 and Inter Europol's #13.

chapters.title: A first for Norma
text: Capo and Creed gave the Norma M30 its first LMP3 win in the world, and the first ELMS victory for the chassis, which now sits alongside the Ginetta and the Ligier on the series' list of LMP3 winners. M.Racing - YMR was only the third team to take an LMP3 1-2 in ELMS, after LNT in 2015 and United in 2016. Cougnaud, Jung and Ricci were second in the Ligier and the Lahayes and Heriau third.

For United it was a day of lost chances: Boyd's #3 was fourth, and the #2 that had won at Silverstone dropped to ninth in class after the clash and gearbox trouble. Sixteen cars were classified; Cool Racing's #4, Oregon's #10 and By Speed Factory's #5 were 13, 19 and 22 laps behind the winner, and AT Racing's #9 was not classified. The next round is at the Red Bull Ring on 23 July.

facts.t: First win for the Norma M30
facts.v: The #19 victory was the first for the Norma M30 chassis, and YMR became the third team to score an LMP3 1-2 in ELMS.
Boyd's 1:45.725 put the United #3 narrowly ahead of Capo's Norma, with the top six inside half a second.

one.label: DailySportsCar: Guibbert Puts GRAFF On Pole For 4H Monza

facts.v: Every Full Course Yellow of the four hours was caused by an LMP3 incident.
Boyd's fourth place was as close as United came; the notebook calls it the first ELMS race the team has started without a podium.

LMGTE.title: JMW's last 458 wins as pole-sitting Ferrari retires
LMGTE.dek: Smith, Fannin and Cocker's JMW Ferrari 458 won by 7.962s from TF Sport's Aston Martin after Spirit of Race's pole-sitting #55 retired with engine failure; Beechdean was third.

chapters.title: A Corvette joins, a 458 says goodbye
text: Seven GTE cars lined up for the second round, one more than at Silverstone, where TF Sport's #90 Aston Martin had dominated qualifying and the race for its first ELMS class win. Larbre Competition added a yellow-and-black Corvette C7.R for a one-off appearance, with Philippon and Brandela joined by Fernando Rees, the former Aston Martin factory driver, who had never driven the car for Larbre before Friday's first session. JMW Motorsport brought the #66 Ferrari 458 Italia for the last time before its new 488 GTE arrived for Le Mans, with Cocker replacing Butcher for the weekend.

The balance of performance targeted the Astons, TF Sport's #90 and Beechdean's #99 gaining a small weight break but losing 1mm from the air restrictor. Practice showed a field in flux: Cairoli's Proton Porsche led Friday on 1:49.943, with Rees only 0.027 behind on his first run in the Corvette. On Saturday morning Rees went fastest on 1:49.164, 0.091 ahead of Thiim's Aston, before Yoluc stopped the TF Sport car at the first chicane after sticking it on a kerb, which brought out a Full Course Yellow.

chapters.title: Griffin puts Ferrari on top
text: Griffin was the clear pole-sitter with a 1:48.027 for Spirit of Race's #55 Ferrari 488 GTE, more than a quarter of a second clear of the field. He said he used a new set of tyres and attacked from the start. Rees took the Corvette to second on 1:48.293, a fine result in what was only the car's second day on the circuit, and Cairoli's Proton Porsche was third on 1:48.514.

TF Sport's Thiim was fourth, the best of the Astons, and Bertolini put the second Spirit of Race Ferrari, the #51, fifth. JMW's #66, driven by Cocker, qualified sixth of seven on 1:49.644 and Gunn's Beechdean Aston was last on 1:49.833, which meant the eventual winner and third-placed finisher began the race at the back of the class.

chapters.title: Proton leads, then #55 takes over
text: The early running was fluid. Proton's Porsche led first, but a long stop dropped it down the order, and Scott fought the #55 Ferrari to the front. Fannin started the #66 and dropped into the pack, then picked off the other GTE cars to run a strong third before handing over to Smith. Rees held a place in the mix with the Corvette despite a spin avoiding the LMP3 clash ahead of him, but his co-drivers could not match his pace and the Larbre car slid back as the other teams brought their professionals into the cars. Bertolini worked the #51 up the order.
Around half-distance the #55, under Cameron, stopped for good with an engine failure, after only 55 laps. Smith, who had passed Brandela's Corvette on track, inherited the lead.

chapters.title: Cocker holds the gap
text: Cocker took over the lead car and managed the gap to Thiim, who was now charging in the #90. TF Sport's Aston Martin climbed into contention in the second half, Thiim and then Hankey closing on the Ferrari, while Beechdean's #99 ran a quiet race in third.

chapters.title: Seven seconds
text: Fannin took the car back for the final stint and brought it home 7.962 seconds clear of Hankey's TF Sport Aston Martin, which had come close but faded in the closing stages. Beechdean's #99, shared by Howard, Gunn and Turner, finished around 30 seconds behind the other Aston to complete the podium. Spirit of Race's #51 was fourth and Proton's Porsche fifth, with Larbre's Corvette sixth.

chapters.title: Sendoff for the 458
text: JMW's win closed an eight-victory ELMS career for the 458 Italia GTE, which had also won at its first race, Paul Ricard in 2011, and had taken the 2012 class title. Cocker kept his record of never having finished off the podium in the car. The team's new Ferrari 488 GTE was due at Le Mans, where Smith would be joined by Stevens and Vanthoor in the GTE Am class.

TF Sport's second place followed its Silverstone win, and Beechdean, the defending champions, was third for the second round running. Spirit of Race, which had left Monza with a retired pole-sitter, was down to the #51 in fourth. The class returns at the Red Bull Ring on 23 July.

facts.v: Spirit of Race's #55 Ferrari stopped around half-distance with an engine failure, handing the lead to the JMW 458.

facts.v: The 458 took wins at its first race (Paul Ricard 2011) and its final one with JMW at Monza, eight ELMS victories in all.
